A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ACCO work, with matching experiments, theory, and appendices. Text extraction, embedded figures, and visual inspection support reliable comparison despite repagination and Figure 6's clipping in v2.

before.justification: Sections 4.1–4.6 and Appendix A report original training, perplexity, timing, delayed-update, and heterogeneous-worker experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains the original empirical results, including TinyStories and OpenWebText training, Alpaca fine-tuning, LAMBADA evaluation, and supplementary experiments.

M1.justification: The two-stage accumulation mechanism, parameter updates, optimizer sharding, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Batch-size clarification and simplified stream terminology do not alter the procedure.

E1.justification: TinyStories, OpenWebText, LAMBADA, Alpaca, communication profiling, and homogeneous and simulated heterogeneous GPU scenarios are retained without changes in coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds ZeRO-2 and ZeRO-3 to the analytical characteristics and memory comparison. This does not introduce new training experiments; the empirical comparator sets involving DDP/ZeRO-1, DPU, and WP remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Model sizes, hardware configurations, training budgets, batch sizes, accumulation settings, preprocessing, and metrics match across versions. The added batch-size explanation clarifies the existing convention rather than reporting a changed protocol.

E4.justification: The DPU warmup and extended-training tests, WP comparison, half-batch experiment in Figure 10, heterogeneous-worker analysis in Figure 9, and profiling in Figure 13 are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Checklist item 7 removes the assertion that large-scale runs are deterministic. TinyStories averaging over three runs and the uncertainty displays remain unchanged; no additional runs or statistical procedures are reported.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds analytical memory estimates of 16 GB for ZeRO-2 and 2 GB for ZeRO-3 at the existing illustrative setting of 64 workers and 7.5B parameters. Existing entries, including ACCO's 46 GB, and all experimental loss, perplexity, and timing results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical setup, Propositions 3.1–3.2, Lyapunov function, convergence bounds, and Appendix A.2 proofs are unchanged. Adding 'SGD, for simplicity' makes the existing scope explicit.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about communication overlap, optimizer sharding, delay compensation, SGD convergence, and training speedups without sacrificing convergence quality.

C2.justification: The checklist replaces the explicit limitation concerning arbitrary delays and crashing GPUs with a reference to Table 1's tradeoffs. Its broader-impacts answer also changes from Yes, with an efficiency/misuse rationale, to NA. Interpretations of the experimental findings remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 3.2 explicitly clarifies that ACCO's batch size counts samples processed between successive parameter updates. This adds technical clarification, while hardware, precision, hyperparameters in Tables 4–5, configuration contents, and code/data access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Table 1 broadens positioning against the ZeRO family by including ZeRO-2 and ZeRO-3 and their lower analytical memory requirements. These use the existing ZeRO citation; the bibliography and related-work prose otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 expands the checklist questions and guidelines, adds short method clarifications, simplifies stream terminology, and updates the contact address and conference notice. The main narrative and section hierarchy are retained.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains two rows and Figure 2's caption is extended. Figure 6 is repositioned to eliminate clipping, appendix figures and tables are repacked, and Listing 1 is consolidated onto one page instead of being interrupted by Figure 13.

improvement.justification: The expanded memory comparison and clearer batch-size convention improve interpretability. Moving Figure 6 fully onto the page and consolidating Listing 1 fix concrete readability problems in v2. These limited gains outweigh the weaker limitation disclosure in the checklist; the experimental evidence and convergence theory are unchanged.
